title: Taking a Position with Stance Adverbs

sections.content: You know stance adverbs such as *francamente* and *lamentablemente* from B2 Unit 1: they step outside the action and comment on the whole sentence. At C1 you use them to take a position in a text that wants to persuade. A leading article (*el editorial*) does not hide its view. It says how sure it is and asks the reader to follow. *Evidentemente* and *a todas luces* present your view as plain to anyone who looks, so they carry weight, and they make a promise: the next words must show why. Use *sin duda* for "beyond doubt" and *francamente* when you want to be direct. Like the adverbs of B2 Unit 1, they stay between commas wherever they stand. An editorial keeps to one per sentence.

sections.title: Four ways to commit
rows: Obviously, the measure comes too late. (you treat it as plain to all)
La medida es, a todas luces, insuficiente.
The measure is, clearly, insufficient. (a fixed phrase: any way you look at it)
Sin duda, el centro necesita menos tráfico.
Without doubt, the centre needs less traffic. (beyond doubt)
Frankly, I see no other solution. (direct, personal)

items.spanish: Evidentemente, la circulación en el centro histórico no puede seguir así.
items.english: Obviously, the traffic in the historic centre cannot go on like this.

items.spanish: La zona peatonal es, a todas luces, una buena idea.
items.english: The pedestrian zone is, clearly, a good idea.

items.spanish: Sin duda, el editorial toma partido.
items.english: Without doubt, the editorial takes sides.

items.spanish: Francamente, nadie ha explicado por qué esperar.
items.english: Frankly, nobody has explained why we should wait.

sections.content: English speakers use "obviously" as a filler and often pile several up. In Spanish an editorial uses one, and it must be the adverb, not the adjective: *Evidente, la medida llega tarde* is wrong. Write *Evidentemente, …* or *Es evidente que…*. And a stance adverb is a promise: if the next sentence does not back it up, the reader stops trusting you.
